title: Re-entrant p-wave superconductivity in a Chern Dartboard Insulator
authors: Yueyang Wu, Rebecca Chan, Taylor L. Hughes, Philip W. Phillips
abstract: We formulate an exact theory for a 2-band superconductor with inter-orbital pairing and band Hatsugai-Kohmoto (HK) interactions. We apply this theory to a Chern dartboard insulator and compute the pair susceptibility and pair correlations analytically. We find that in the insulating phase previously predicted by BCS theory (small pairing strength $g$, chemical potential $μ$ in the gap), the HK interaction can induce superconductivity, and possibly a Chern dartboard superconductor, by lifting the doubly-occupied band and making it cross the chemical potential. From this HK-induced superconductor, we notice that in a significant parameter range (HK interaction strength $U = 1$, $μ= 0.5$), an insulator-superconductor-insulator re-entrant transition exists. We isolate the re-entrance to a conflation between HK interactions and inter-orbital pairings.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes superconductivity in a Chern Dartboard Insulator coupled with strong electron-electron interactions (HK coupling). The authors demonstrate that these interactions can induce superconductivity even in insulating regimes and predict a unique re-entrant superconducting phase. The mechanism hinges on the non-monotonic temperature dependence of the pairing susceptibility, a signature of the combined effects of correlation and pairing.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence of re-entrant p-wave superconductivity in a Chern Dartboard Insulator (CDI) when strong electron-electron interactions are included.
main_result: The system exhibits a novel insulator-superconductor-insulator re-entrant transition, which is attributed to the confluence of Hund's coupling (HK) interactions and inter-orbital pairing terms.
method: The authors employ an exact theoretical formulation using a 2-band generalization of the Hatsugai-Kohmoto model, calculating the pair susceptibility via Dyson equations and mean-field theory.
model_or_system: The model is a 2-band superconductor built upon the Chern Dartboard Insulator (CDI) platform, incorporating both inter-orbital pairing and band Hatsugai-Kohmoto (HK) interactions.
key_observables: Pair susceptibility ($\chi$), superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), and the existence of re-entrant transitions in the phase diagram.
important_parameters: HK interaction strength ($U$), chemical potential ($\mu$), and pairing strength ($g$).
main_assumptions: The analysis utilizes a $p$-wave pairing structure and relies on a 2-band generalization of the HK model Green function.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the band structure changes due to HK interaction, phase diagrams showing superconducting regions, and plots of the pairing susceptibility ($\chi_0(T)$) demonstrating non-monotonic behavior leading to re-entrance.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the model Hamiltonian and calculating the bare pairing susceptibility ($\chi_0$). It then uses mean-field theory to find the gap self-consistency, culminating in the detailed analysis of $\chi_0(T)$ to pinpoint the re-entrant transition mechanism.
why_interesting: The mechanism of re-entrance arising from the non-monotonic temperature dependence of the pairing susceptibility, driven by both correlation (HK) and pairing terms, offers insights into complex superconducting phase diagrams beyond simple BCS predictions.
